messages.content: 你能幫我為我和朋友共10位計劃在華盛頓州西雅圖的一天嗎？我們都是美食愛好者，想要嘗試一些海鮮和意大利菜作為午餐。晚上，我們有興趣參加一場音樂會或體育賽事。你能幫我找到適合我們的餐廳和活動嗎？

function.name: restaurant_find_group
function.description: Find restaurants suitable for groups based on specified criteria such as location and cuisine. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Seattle, WA

cuisine.description: Preferred cuisine at the restaurant. Default is all if not specified.

group_size.description: Size of the group that the restaurant should accommodate.

function.name: events_find_event
function.description: Find events suitable for groups based on specified criteria such as location and event type. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state, e.g. Seattle, WA

event_type.description: Type of event. Default is all if not specified.

group_size.description: Size of the group that the event should accommodate.

message.reasoning:
The user wants a plan for a day in Seattle for 10 people, food lovers, lunch with seafood and Italian, and evening music or sports event. They want to find suitable restaurants and events. We have two functions: restaurant_find_group and events_find_event. We need to call them. For restaurants: location "Seattle, WA", cuisine options: "Seafood" and "Italian". But the function expects cuisine?: "Seafood" | "Italian" | "Chinese"[]? Actually the type says cuisine?: "Seafood" | "Italian" | "Chinese"[]. That seems odd: Chinese is an array? Probably a mistake. But we can pass cuisine: ["Seafood", "Italian"]? The type says union of string or array? It says "Chinese"[] meaning array of Chinese? Might be a mistake. We'll just pass cuisine: ["Seafood", "Italian"]. group_size: 10.

For events: location "Seattle, WA", event_type: "Concert" | "Sports" | "Exhibition" | "Festival"[]. We want music concert or sports. So event_type: ["Concert", "Sports"]. group_size: 10.

We need to call both functions. Then produce a plan. We'll call restaurant_find_group first.
